issue.title: test_ppid_walk_teardown_of_starter_descendants_leaves_monitor_running never sees done.json within 10s under the full parallel lane, passes in isolation
issue.description: Flake report: the ppid-walk teardown test in tests/monitor/test_monitor_start_supervisor.py fails intermittently under the full lane and passes alone. See the evidence field for the two candidate causes (SIGTERM-vs-detach race, or a 10s wait too tight under load).

task_type_fields.evidence:
On 2026-09-25 (master f648e88e4 plus an unrelated ACE header-card diff that touches no monitor code), `just check` (monitor y9gc9v3aezt8, sase tool run 945f3a716809a1eed2a035d9e2c5af93) escalated test-scoped to the full lane (11 xdist workers, 47406 items, 23m05s wall). This node was one of two failures out of 47,394 (the other, test_bootstrap_issue_enroll_hello_round_trip_through_real_gateway, is already tracked as sase-13h):

    tests/monitor/_fixtures.py:177: AssertionError
    monitor at .../popen-gw6/test_ppid_walk_teardown_of_sta0/.sase/projects/proj/artifacts/ace-run/202609/25/20260925110654 never finished

The failing line is `done = wait_for_done(record.artifacts_dir, timeout=10.0)` in tests/monitor/test_monitor_start_supervisor.py: no `done.json` appeared within 10 s of the test SIGTERMing every descendant of the pytest worker.

Serial reproduction: none. Re-run alone on the same unchanged tree (`pytest -n0`, project defaults) it passed in 13.16s (this node: 5.56s setup, 3.79s call). Fail rate: 1 of 1 observed full-lane runs of this tree; earlier runs of the same tree family in this session did not fail it, so it is intermittent under load.

Two candidate causes, neither confirmed:

1. Race. `_signal_descendants(os.getpid(), SIGTERM)` runs immediately after `start_monitor` returns and signals every process still in the worker's ppid tree. If the supervisor has not yet detached (setsid / reparent) or installed its SIGTERM handling when the signal lands, it dies and never writes `done.json`. Host contention widens that window. The assertion message would look identical to a slow run.
2. Budget. The wait is 10 s while the fixture default POLL_TIMEOUT is 60 s, and the call alone takes 3.79 s on an idle host, so a saturated host can exceed 10 s legitimately.

To tell them apart, capture the supervisor's exit status and supervisor log when `done.json` is missing (today the assertion reports only the artifacts dir), and re-run the node in a loop under `stress`-style CPU load with the wait raised to 60 s: a pass means budget, a persistent failure means the SIGTERM race.
task_type_fields.repro_cmd: just check-full (or a loaded just test-scoped), then isolated: .venv/bin/python -m pytest -n0 tests/monitor/test_monitor_start_supervisor.py::test_ppid_walk_teardown_of_starter_descendants_leaves_monitor_running -q
